messages:
maria: thinking out loud — for the routing quota tweaks next week, can we use a lightweight 'probe' phase instead of full canary? want to send a tiny fraction of traffic with new config and validate metrics before wide activation
lee: +1 to probes if we can make them observable. what exactly do you mean by 'probe'? percent rollout or synthetic probing?
maria: both options on table. idea A: 0.5% live traffic routed by policy 'probe=true' A/B. Idea B: scheduled synthetic probes hitting the same code paths (batch ingress + real KV cache)
jon: real traffic catches more oddness (client headers, edge cases) but has higher blast radius. synthetic is safer but we need parity. could we do a hybrid?
priya: hybrid seems good. small live percentage + a parallel synthetic harness that mirrors requests and checks outputs. telemetry should gate the next step automatically.
carla: agree. we need a clear fail condition in the console and an automatic rollback trigger. propose metrics: config_probe_error_rate > 0.5% OR latency_p95 regression > 150ms over baseline for 5m
maria: noted. also UX question: should the console expose a 'start probe' button with configurable duration/percent, or only allow via API?
lee: ops will want console button for quick checks. api-only for infra-as-code flows is still required. simplest: both, but console should prefill the api payload and show dry-run diff
jon: implementation detail debate: endpoint name `configs.apply` vs `configs.activate`. `apply` sounds idempotent and safe, `activate` implies immediate effect. I lean towards `apply` for probe flow and `promote` for full rollout.
priya: +1 on `apply` + `promote`. also include `dry_run:true` flag to get evaluation without altering routing table.
carla: runtime-bot just posted a runbook snippet earlier, copying it in case helpful:
carla: ```
# probe runbook
1) create probe config with metadata.probe=true and percent=0.5
2) call POST /v1/configs.apply body: {config, dry_run:false}
3) watch metrics: config_probe_error_rate, routing_mismatch_rate, p95_latency
4) if thresholds exceeded -> POST /v1/configs.rollback {id}
```
lee: can we add a telemetry tag so we can slice metrics by probe_id? makes dashboards much cleaner.
maria: yes — add `probe_id` header and config annotation. console should surface that probe_id and link to dashboard with prefilters
jon: dashboard note: add a 'probe' panel with time compare, and a small sparkline per route. also show sample failing requests (redacted) for quick triage
priya: question for API design: should probe be a first-class field on the config object or a separate 'probe' resource referencing config_id?
lee: separate resource is nicer for lifecycle (start/stop) and audit. config stays immutable; probe is an action referencing a config version
maria: ok we'll go with probe resource approach. next steps: PR for API schema (open to bikeshedding names), a simple console modal for start/stop, and a telemetry plan with thresholds + alerting rules. can someone draft the API schema?
jon: I'll sketch an OpenAPI snippet later today.
carla: runtime-bot: probe-created event will be emitted when probe starts — planning to wire that into the incident/alerting playbooks
runtime-bot: [automated] emitted event: probe.created id=probe_2026_03_20_01 by maria
lee: awesome. I'll draft the dashboard tiles and alert rules. thanks team, this feels much safer than our previous ad-hoc rollouts :thumbsup:
maria: thanks all — tagging @priya to own the runbook updates and @jon for the API PR. we'll sync on Thurs 10am if no objections
priya: on it.
jon: see you Thurs.
